messages.subject: random intercept linear model
parts:
Dear Stan Users,

I have another Stan newbies question, which in a way is a follow up from my post last week - https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/stan-users/Lindsay/stan-users/fsM8GPG4cpM/T09Y38Rx3MMJ

I am trying to hierarchise a linear model, starting with adding a random intercept. The model has run fine; however when I try to print the output, it doesn't seem to "get" the random intercepts. Perhaps there is something I should be monitoring (via the "parameters" statement) which I am not? Any help greatly appreciated.

Lindsay

My Stan code is as follows:

stan_data <- list("y"=y,
                "year"=year,
                "agency"=agency,
                "N_agencies" = N_agencies,
                "N_obs" = N_obs)


hier_0 <- "data {
                     int<lower=1> N_obs;
                    int<lower=1> N_agencies;
                    int<lower=1, upper=N_agencies> agency;
                    real year[N_obs];
                    real y[N_obs];
                    }
                           
            parameters {
                     real alpha[N_agencies];
                     real beta;
                     real<lower=0, upper=10000000> sigma;
                        }
             
            transformed parameters{

                       }
                      
            model {
                vector[N_obs] mu_hat;

                sigma ~ uniform(0, 100000);
                beta ~ normal(0, 1000);
               
                for(j in 1:N_agencies){
                alpha[j] ~ normal(0, 1000);
                }
                 
   
                for(i in 1:N_obs){
                    mu_hat[i] <- alpha[agency[i]] + beta * year[i];
                       y[i] ~ normal(mu_hat[i], sigma[agency[i]]);
                }     
            }"


    write(lm, file="hier_0")


hier_fit0 <- stan(file="hier_0",
                  data=stan_data,
                  chains=1,
                     iter=5000)


As noted above, the model seems to run fine. However, when I try to print the output I get the following:

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: random intercept linear model
parts:
On Tuesday, February 26, 2013 6:42:01 AM UTC-5, Lindsay wrote:
I am trying to hierarchise a linear model, starting with adding a random intercept. The model has run fine; however when I try to print the output, it doesn't seem to "get" the random intercepts. Perhaps there is something I should be monitoring (via the "parameters" statement) which I am not? Any help greatly appreciated.

Can you post the simulated data also? As far as I know, if you specify the parameter as alpha[N_agencies], the output should always have draws for alpha[1], alpha[2], ... alpha[N_agencies].

Ben

P.S. A faster version of your model follows

hier_0 <- "data {
                     int<lower=1> N_obs;
                    int<lower=1> N_agencies;
                    int<lower=1, upper=N_agencies> agency;
                    real year[N_obs];
                    real y[N_obs];
                    }
                           
            parameters {
                     real alpha[N_agencies];
                     real beta;

real<lower=0, upper=10000000> sigma[N_agencies];
                        }
                                  
            model {
                vector[N_obs] mu_hat;
                   vector[N_obs] sigmas;

                // implicit: sigma ~ uniform(0, 100000);
                beta ~ normal(0, 1000);
                   alpha ~ normal(0,1000); // no explicit loop

for(i in 1:N_obs){
                    mu_hat[i] <- alpha[agency[i]] + beta * year[i];

sigmas[i] <- sigma[agency[i]];
                }
                    y ~ normal(mu_hat, sigmas); // outside of loop
     
            }"

messages.author: 45012a2c12a7d946
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: random intercept linear model
parts:
Thanks Ben (and others),

The model I am trying to run is I guess similar to the one in Gelman and Hill, p. 350---though I have not yet modelled the distribution of the alphas. But this is only by way of a warm up. I am really looking to run something like the one in Shor, Bafumi, Keele and Park (home.uchicago.edu/~bshor/research/tscs.bml.pdf)---except that the covariate(s) I am interested in are at the group (agency) level instead of at the individual level. 

Thinking through the problem a bit more, and taking account of Ben's advice, I realise I should be asking for something a bit more like this:

hier_0 <- "data {
int<lower=1> N_obs;
int<lower=1> N_agencies;
int <lower=1, upper=N_agencies> agency;
        real year[N_obs];
       real y[N_obs];
   }
   
parameters {
    real alpha[N_agencies];
    real beta;

real<lower=0> sigma;
   } 
 
transformed parameters{

  }
 
model {
vector[N_obs] y_hat;

beta ~ normal(0, 1000);
alpha ~ normal(0, 1000);
for(i in 1:N_obs){
y_hat[i] <- alpha[agency[i]] + beta * year[i];
}
 
  y ~ normal(y_hat, sigma); 
  
}"


write(hier_0, file="hier_0")

hier_fit0 <- stan(file="hier_0",
data=stan_data, 
chains=1, 
  iter=5000)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] random intercept linear model
parts:
On 2/26/13 6:42 AM, Lindsay wrote:
> ... however when

> I try to print the output, it doesn't seem to "get" the random intercepts. Perhaps there is something I should be
> monitoring (via the "parameters" statement) which I am not? Any help greatly appreciated.

Only parameters, transformed parameters, and generated
quantities are printed.

Local variables like your mu_hat aren't printed.
If you want it printed, you need to declare it and
define it as a transformed parameter.

> model {
> vector[N_obs] mu_hat;
...

> for(i in 1:N_obs){
> mu_hat[i] <- alpha[agency[i]] + beta * year[i];
> y[i] ~ normal(mu_hat[i], sigma[agency[i]]);
> }
> }

So your transformed parameters block looks like:

transformed parameters {
vector[N_obs] mu_hat;
for(i in 1:N_obs)
mu_hat[i] <- alpha[agency[i]] + beta * year[i]; for (i in
}

and you don't need to declare or define mu_hat in the model block.

- Bob
